name: Kommo
tagline: A sales CRM built around a shared WhatsApp, Instagram and Telegram inbox with pipelines, chatbots and lead automation.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The CRM half of Kommo is genuinely easy: contacts, companies, a drag-and-drop deal pipeline, notes, tasks, a timeline. An agent will hand you that in an afternoon and it will be faster and less cluttered than the real thing. The half you cannot build is the reason people bought it: an official WhatsApp Business channel, Instagram and Facebook DMs, and Telegram all landing in one threaded inbox with templates, chatbots and 24-hour window rules. WhatsApp access runs through Meta and a business solution provider, with app review, template approval, number verification and per-conversation fees, none of which a coding agent can conjure. Build the pipeline if you want a tidy pipeline, but do not pretend you replaced the inbox.
coreLoopDIY: A local CRM with contacts, a kanban deal pipeline, tasks and a per-contact activity timeline, plus one optional Telegram bot channel for inbound messages.
requirements: Python 3.11 and a machine to leave running
A Telegram bot token if you want the one working inbox channel
A tunnel or small VPS if you want Telegram webhooks to reach you
No WhatsApp or Instagram access without a Meta app and a BSP contract
whatYouLose: Official WhatsApp Business API messaging, including template approval and conversation billing
Instagram and Facebook DM threading, which needs Meta app review you will not enjoy
Chatbot builder, drip sequences and lead-capture forms wired to the same pipeline
Mobile apps with push notifications, so replies stop being instant
A shared team inbox with assignment, mentions and answer-time reporting
moatNotes: The integrations here are not REST calls, they are commercial relationships with Meta plus a verified business identity per phone number.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the customers are already in WhatsApp and Instagram, and being the business that can legally and reliably answer there is the product. Kommo sits between messy consumer messaging apps and a pipeline, absorbs the approval paperwork, and gives a small sales team one place to answer from a phone. A self-hosted kanban board does not move a single conversation off a salesperson's personal phone, which is the actual problem being solved.
notes: The pipeline is a weekend; the WhatsApp channel is a contract. The moat is privileged, reviewed access to Meta's messaging platforms plus the switching cost of years of conversation history living inside it.
prompt:
Build a local-first personal sales CRM in an empty folder. It copies Kommo's pipeline and contact model and deliberately skips the messaging platforms.

Stack, no substitutions: Python 3.11, FastAPI, SQLite through SQLModel, server-rendered Jinja2 templates, HTMX for interactions, one hand-written CSS file. No React, no build step, no cloud services, no telemetry, no login screen. It runs on localhost with `uvicorn app:app --reload`.

Data model: Contact (name, company, phone, email, tags, source, created_at), Deal (title, contact_id, value, currency, stage, status of open/won/lost, close_date), Note (contact_id, body, created_at), Task (contact_id or deal_id, title, due_date, done), Message (contact_id, channel, direction, body, sent_at).

Screens:
1. Pipeline board: columns from an editable list of stages, deal cards draggable between stages via HTMX post, stage totals in the header, filter by tag and by owner-free text search.
2. Contact list with search, and a contact detail page showing a single merged timeline of notes, messages, tasks and deal stage changes, newest first.
3. Deal detail page with inline edit, win and lose buttons that stamp a reason.
4. Today view: overdue and due-today tasks across all contacts.

Optional single channel: if TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN is set in .env, expose POST /webhook/telegram that stores inbound messages as Message rows, auto-creating a Contact on first contact, and add a reply box on the contact page that calls sendMessage. If the token is missing, hide the reply box and keep everything else working. Read all secrets from .env via python-dotenv and commit a .env.example only.

Also include: CSV import for contacts with a column-mapping step, CSV export of contacts and deals, a seed script with about 30 fake contacts and 15 deals, and a single-file SQLite database at ./data/crm.db.

Explicitly out of scope, do not stub or fake: WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook Messenger, email sending, chatbot builders, multi-user accounts, permissions, mobile apps.

Finish with a README that states the run command, the .env keys, and one blunt paragraph saying this is a pipeline tool and not an omnichannel inbox.
